summary: The team is executing a China-first global marketing push behind Asia Star and Intelligent China while finalising the Knowledge website redesign, and this week's urgent work is a mix of design sign-off and a cluster of near-term content and event deliverables.
summaryDetail: The dominant initiative is the seven-month SEO/AI-search visibility strategy, which has locked in Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two programs to promote, with Berkeley folded into the audit phase and Stanford/Columbia parked for now; Joseph still owes the areas/prompts focus document and participant/CRM analysis, and the team needs the SEO manager's conversion-tracking brief to make it measurable. The Knowledge website redesign is at a decision point: the team has endorsed keeping the two-menu structure and bringing BCI/BSI indices into the Knowledge section, and now needs a 30-minute working session (Joseph, Julie, team lead) to mark specific design feedback so Joker can implement changes. This week also carries a hard deadline cluster around the Nov 27 Cartier Women's Initiative roundtable at the Beijing campus, the Women in Leadership Forum emcee script review (Kaylee and Xuan), and the ESG report final draft that Ira must assemble from Joseph's and Julie's comments. On the content side, the Intelligent China webpage must be completed, the MBZUAI Academy thank-you piece needs publishing under School News, and the Asia Start videos need student amplification now that the standalone videos section is being dissolved and dispersed by topic. Looking ahead, Ira, Joseph and Julie need to convene early next week on the 2027 SEO/GEO/SEM and third-party costs proposal, which ties into the email platform and budget review where 9,618 unsubscribed entries were already archived across five Mailchimp audiences.
